_about: Ours, not a design copy. The post-Trial crackdown (scenes crackdown_street and crackdown_lantern), the shut Trial Hall, the curfew order until the pick (POST_TRIAL_CRACKDOWN §5: posts, notice, cordon, Glimmerwell on the east road; townsfolk back by day once Ilse calls, D1405), Warden Ilse's call (ilse_call) and the Lodge debrief (warden_meet) from RENDEZVOUS_VINCENT beats 1-2 (D1395, D1404; merged with WARDEN_SUMMONS by Vincent). The rendezvous, the two shifts and the report are a later build on top of this one, which moves the pick gate to story.rdv_done. Lantern House room objects live in fernbrook_rooms.json, because its maps load after every detail patch.
_placeholders: Every line here is PLACEHOLDER for June (D1208). The Commander is unnamed (D1198). 'Keeper tank' wording and the tanks' look are drafts (D1202). The Warden's lines and the dawn wire are placeholders until WARDEN_SUMMONS is written and settled (D1396-D1418). story.fen_lean steps (+1 Keep it, +1 He's hiding something, -1 He means well, 0 Hand it over) are PLACEHOLDER until Seals lore v3.1's encoding lands (D1411). Story's lines (STORY_LINES Nov 4, 2026) are final for the Hall door's denyFirst (D2133), Fen's fen_dawn lines (D2134) and the Warden's call and Amos's message (D2139).

crackdown_street: A white beam slides up the road. Then the ground starts to hum.
By order of High Charity, this square is closed. Everyone home. Now.
Right here. Signed in the capital, stamped and current.
The Commander reads it under the tank's lamp, then hands it back.
Permit's in order. Your stand can stay. The square still closes.
A curfew's no good for business. We'll set up out on the east road tonight.
Holder. This Hall is shut. Unvetted holders were tested here.
A Seal is the Keepers' to give, {name}. And ours to take back.
Take it, then. Watch it go dull in your hand. It knows whose it is.
The Seal sits in the Commander's glove. Its shine goes out.
Dull as a button. Keep your trinket.
The Seal hums. Then it's quiet.
Commander. Stand down. That Seal was won fair, in my Hall, in front of my roots.
Master Fen. Your Hall is closed.
{name}. Go to the Lantern House. Amos will keep you. I'll be right behind you.
Brighter by nature! Find us on the east road, Fernbrook!
You can't shut a Trial Hall! Glimmerwell would never lock a town indoors!
Out after my order, and shouting at my Keepers. Take that one in.
A Keeper leads the Junior Bright away down the west road. Their Walkling trots close behind.
Orders came from over my head, citizen. Go on in. Keep your head down.
crackdown_lantern: You'll stay in here tonight, holder. You can't leave.
Can't leave? A Lantern House is for rest, not for keeping people. On what law?
The Commander's word is the law tonight.
Then let's settle it the old way. Your Walkling and mine, right here.
Nobody battles in my town tonight.
New order. You and Master Fen stay in this house tonight. Step out before dawn, and you're both arrested.
You'd arrest a Hall Master in her own town? Listen to yourself.
A Seal says a holder can help run things here. Fernbrook doesn't need the help.
The Seal only matters if you comply.
And stay clear of Glimmerwell. Folk who help them get a name for it. Then we come asking.
Hush, all of you. The wire's on.
Block News, evening edition. We go now to the capital.
The picture flickers and cuts to the President.
Good evening, Fernbrook. For your safety, a curfew is in force tonight.
So, from tonight, Fernbrook keeps a curfew from dusk to dawn. Stay in. Keep your Walklings close.
And no new Seals will be given in Fernbrook until further notice. A Seal is a promise. We keep it carefully.
Every Seal ever earned is written down in High Charity, as it was in the Great War. It will stay that way.
A Seal is not for sale. Not to anyone. Remember that.
The Keepers keep you, and I keep the Keepers. Good night. Be kind in the streets.
Not for sale. Then who's been buying?
Maybe. He's always sounded kind. Kind isn't the same as right.
Careful who hears you say that. ...But I heard it too.
They can't take the one you've earned, {name}. Hold onto that.
Dusk to dawn. Not a minute before.
I'm writing to the Warden tonight. A Commander doesn't outrank the lantern's law.
The beds are made. Rest your team. I'll keep the lamp low.
At dawn the curfew lifts. Fen and {name} are let go.
I asked them for help with the Amberwild. They sent boots. I won't forget it.
{name}. Warden Ilse sent word down the wire for you. She wants you home at the Lodge.
The Warden read my letter, then. Go. I'll be at the orchard gate.
warden_meet: {name}. Sit down. I had Fen's letter, and I heard the President's broadcast with everyone else.
Tanks in Fen's town. A Trial Hall shut. And not one Warden asked. Not one.
The Keepers are not that order. Someone dusted off an old law from the war.
Fen wrote to me before they shut her door. Walklings walking off at night, near Wickerglen.
Glimmerwell's tents are shut to a Warden. I know someone who walks where I can't.
Jacob Chi. No phone, no side. Past the fallen trunk at Wickerglen's east edge. Say I sent you.
warden_after: Jacob Chi. Past the fallen trunk at Wickerglen's east edge. Say I sent you.
ilse_call: Your Keeper1 buzzes in your pocket. WARDEN ILSE.
{name}? Fen's letter reached me. I know what happened in Fernbrook last night.
Come home to the Lodge. Not on the wire.
